name: Brule Lake
summary: Cook County, MN tower near Brule Lake; reported smoke in 1936 and was later taken down. Undated pages report steel, a stair section and an anchor pad on the site.
design: Steel tower with a cab much larger than typical Minnesota towers and a deck running around the cap (1966 photograph)
status_note: Taken down before 2012 per a forum post; removal date not found. An undated local history page reports steel, a stair section and an anchor pad on the site.
agency: U.S. Forest Service (owner listed as USFS in the Cook County survey)

access.note: No closure or permit is described in the sources read. The old trail was hard to find on a 2020 trip (trip report).

visit.trail_note: No standing tower is described at the site. A 2020 trip report found the trail almost impossible to find and unmaintained for about a decade.

events.note: Survey notes from 1934 and 1958 place a survey station near the center of the tower base

Brule Lake Lookout and Kelso Lookout reported smoke at about the same time on July 11, after an unusually hot afternoon; comparing the two reports placed the fire near the portage between Gordon and Cherokee lakes
Brule Lake Lookout reported smoke in the 1936 fire season
Photograph shows the steel tower with an unusually large cab and a deck around the cap
